name: Vynody
one_liner: A light, good-looking local music player with word-by-word lyrics and serverless sync across devices on your network.

text.why: Players for downloaded music look and behave differently on every device. Vynody aims to give Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS and Android the same experience.
text.take: On Windows it can output in WASAPI Exclusive mode, bypassing the system mixer.
build: Auto-filled tags and artwork (AcoustID, MusicBrainz), LRCLIB lyric search, AI-generated word-by-word lyrics, LAN sync of tracks and playlists, connections to Navidrome, Jellyfin, WebDAV and SMB, and a live spectrum display.

who.role: People who listen to their own music files instead of streaming.

start.text: Get the build for your device from the repository's Releases; Microsoft Store and App Store (macOS, iOS) versions also exist.

caveat: Licensed GPL-3.0. The author says it was built with AI-assisted 'vibe coding', and it is a young project with about 130 stars. Which service powers the AI lyric generation is not stated in the README.

license.scope_text: Use freely. Release your source if you redistribute (copyleft).

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

images.alt: The Vynody player: album art on the left, the track title, waveform progress bar and playback controls on the right, and a spectrum along the bottom.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
